summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not an `Exception`.
description: The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with an `Exception` excluded from its type.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonException(new Error()); // => new Error()
requireNonException({}); // => {}
requireNonException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
